messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — seeing steady resident memory creep on long streaming tool-loop jobs (~3–6h). Not a hard OOM but ~4–5% resident gain per hour on prod-serving-1 after the 2.4.1 rollout. Dumped a few counters and heap samples.
ops-bot: [alert] memory-resident-increase on prod-serving-1 (metric: rss) — triggered at 2423456700
jon: Can you paste pmap/top and the KV residency counters? Also which model variant & kernel were used?
maria: model: redwood/open-chat-xl-q4f; kernel: fused-attn-short (auto-chosen). pmap snapshot + kv stats below:

```
PID   RSS     VSZ     CMD
3241  1.2G   6.4G   /srv/redwood/serve --runtime

KV_STATS: resident=1.20GB -> 1.56GB over 4h
kv_entries=1.2M evicted=12.3k reuse_hits=58k reuse_rate=0.048
page_frag_ratio=0.27 slab_allocs=234k slab_frag_bytes=128MB
```

maria: interesting bit — evict_count is non-zero but reuse_rate low, and slab_frag_bytes increased steadily. Not typical leak (no growing unique keys), more like residency/fragmentation.
lee: Could be allocator fragmentation + many small pinned KV spans. Any change to kernel selection or batching heuristics around the same time?
cassandra: Yes — the kernel selection tweak (short-seq fused-attn) and a batching window increase were rolled two days before the symptom start. Both touched request lifetime and intra-batch KV residency.
maria: timeline matches. Also saw more long-lived prefix cache entries for tool-loop routes (tools re-entrant calls keep prefixes pinned).
ev an: From quick heap profile (heap-prof-2423456802) I see many small objects from kv_span_t with refcounts stuck at 1 and not being reaped until explicit eviction. Flame excerpt:

```
# top symbols
kv_span_alloc  32%
kv_lookup      18%
slab_alloc     12%
batch_processor 10%
```

ev an: suggests allocations are concentrated in KV spans and slab allocator, not native leak in model weights.
jon: Have we tried a canary with aggressive eviction TTL or disabling prefix caching for the route?
maria: Pushed a canary config: prefix_cache.ttl=60s, prefix_cache.enabled=false for route /tools/exec and set kv.eviction.scan_interval=30s. Also added periodic slab.compact() every 30m in runtime config.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started on prod-serving-1 (canary id c-2423456920)
ops-bot: Monitoring: rss, kv_resident, slab_frag, reuse_rate
maria: After ~6h on canary: resident growth slowed from 4–5%/hr -> ~0.8%/hr. slab_frag_bytes flatlined. Preliminary looks like cache TTL + compaction helps.
lee: That points to reuse/retention rather than true leak. Two follow-ups: 1) instrument kernel selection path so KV refs from kernel buffers get weak refs instead of strong; 2) re-evaluate batching window logic — long contexts keep batches open and may extend KV lifetime.
cassandra: Also schedule a full 24h heap profile with jemalloc background thread off to rule out allocator heuristics.
ev an: Quick note — batching heuristic: for long-context streaming we currently extend internal batch window up to 250ms; that increases concurrent KV residency. Try reducing to 100ms for streaming-tool-loop class.
maria: Filed PR: #987 "kv: ensure ephemeral kernel-side refs use weak handles" (link: http://go/repo/pr/987) — @lee can you review? Also PR #988 for runtime config defaults: reduce streaming batch window to 100ms.
jon: I'll run an AB test comparing batch window 100 vs 250ms for throughput/latency and mem growth across 8h runs.
maria: Added a lightweight diagnostic endpoint to dump kv residency histogram: /_debug/kv_residency

```
# sample output
bucket[0-64B]=42% bucket[64-256B]=30% bucket[256-1KB]=15% bucket[1KB+]=13%
oldest_entry_age=4h avg_age=12m
```

maria: TL;DR so far: patterns point to increased KV residency due to batching + prefix caching changes; compaction + lower TTL helps. Kernel selection may exacerbate by holding refs inside fused kernels. Next steps: deeper 24h heap profile, merge weak-ref PR, run AB with new batch window, and monitor.
ev an: ack, scheduling 24h profile starting 2423470000.
lee: I'll double-check kernel runtime doesn't pin pointers in the JIT path; if it does we should fence the KV lifetime.
jon: I'll coordinate AB & perf dashboards. If this fixes it we should backport to 2.4.2 patch.
maria: Thanks all — will post follow-ups once 24h profile is in. :thumbsup:
